subject: Budget range validation - NovaAI token volumes & procurement thresholds
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@novaai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-10T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: token volumes & procurement thresholds

Alex — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned:

What I heard:
- NovaAI is expecting production traffic in two phases: initial ramp (3–6 months) then steady-state.
- Estimated token volume: ~200M – 800M tokens/month (varies by feature rollout).
- Procurement: procurement team indicated a PO requirement and an approval threshold; you said procurement will escalate if monthly spend > $25k.
- Target economics: your internal goal is to keep unit spend low; you mentioned an aspiration around $50–$75 per 1M tokens but wanted to validate with committed pricing.

Open asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the expected monthly token band (low / mid / high) for the first 6 months and which band procurement will sign off on?
2) Confirm procurement threshold for requiring formal PO and any term requirements for discounts (e.g., 12-month minimum).
3) I'll send a couple of committed pricing options and a one-page pricing sheet — can you share whether procurement wants SOW + PO or DocuSign contract first?

Attaching: novaai-token-estimates.csv (your export from the call) and a short draft SOW.

If we can get procurement confirmation today, I can put together a 2-tier committed offer (200M and 800M) with corresponding $/1M token pricing for your review.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0143

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@novaai.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: NovaAI Procurement <procurement@novaai.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token volumes & procurement thresholds

Thanks Laura — good summary. A few clarifications from procurement / product: 

- Monthly token estimate: current internal plan is 200M (pilot) -> 500M (expanded) -> up to ~800M as we launch feature set across customers. For first 3 months we expect 200M–350M; months 4–6 we could be 400M–600M depending on adoption.
- Procurement thresholds: procurement requires a PO for any vendor spend > $25,000/month. For discounts, procurement generally prefers a 12-month minimum commitment for tiered pricing; 3-month pilots are fine but would be priced at standard committed rates or slightly higher.
- Approval cadence: procurement can fast-track PO within 7–10 business days if SOW + pricing are provided and legal has a short review.
- Our internal target for vendor unit economics is $50/1M tokens but team is open to negotiated committed pricing if there are clear performance SLAs and uplift for longer terms.

Procurement (cc'd) — can you confirm if a 6-12 month term with PO is the preferred route for getting committed pricing?

Best,
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, NovaAI
alex.johnson@novaai.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-10T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap — quick pricing calc (internal)

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Alex's note. Quick thoughts on two offer structures to cover their bands and procurement constraints:

1) Pilot-commit (3 months) — conservative
- Minimum committed: 200M tokens/month
- Price: $80 / 1M tokens
- Estimated monthly cost: (200 * $80) / 1M -> $16,000/month
- Notes: short term pilot, no 12-month obligation, procurement can issue PO for pilot.

2) Committed annual (preferred for discounts) — scale
- Minimum committed: 800M tokens/month (or annualized commitment across months)
- Price: $60 / 1M tokens (with SLA & higher support)
- Estimated monthly cost: (800 * $60) / 1M -> $48,000/month
- Notes: requires 12-month commitment for discount; procurement indicated PO > $25k/month, so this will push standard procurement review (but they said fast-track possible).

Also include an intermediate option: 400M @ $70 / 1M -> ~$28k/month which sits just above procurement PO threshold and might be easiest to get procurement approval for a 6–12 month term.

Request: Marissa, can you prepare a redlined pricing sheet (two columns: pilot vs committed) and a short SOW with onboarding milestones? Rishi — can you run the unit-econ sanity check on $60–$80/1M against our cost model and confirm margin at those tiers?

I'll send the external email with the pricing sheet and SOW once we align internally.

Thanks — Laura

Subject: Proposed budget bands & next steps (pricing sheet + SOW attached)

Alex / Procurement — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on the call and internal alignment, here are three proposed options to cover NovaAI's expected ramp: 

Option A — Pilot (3 months)
- Committed min: 200M tokens/month
- Price: $78 / 1M tokens
- Est. monthly: $15,600
- Term: 3 months, PO acceptable

Option B — Mid (6–12 months)
- Committed min: 400M tokens/month
- Price: $70 / 1M tokens
- Est. monthly: $28,000
- Term: 6–12 months, PO + SOW preferred

Option C — Annual Committed
- Committed min: 800M tokens/month
- Price: $60 / 1M tokens
- Est. monthly: $48,000
- Term: 12 months, PO + SOW required, SLA & priority support included

Procurement note: you mentioned PO requirement at > $25k/mo. Option B and C exceed that threshold; procurement (cc'd) — if you can confirm the exact docs and expected timeline for PO issuance, we will produce a DocuSign contract + SOW and can target onboarding within 2 weeks of PO.

Next steps:
- Procurement: confirm PO process / required docs and lead time.
- Alex: confirm which option you'd like to pilot (A/B/C) and whether you prefer DocuSign or PO-first flow.
- Laura/Redwood: we'll send the redlined pricing-sheet and SOW; Marissa will include a comparison table with unit economics and estimated savings vs pay-as-you-go.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf, sow-draft.docx

If this looks good I'll prepare a short email to procurement summarizing the paperwork they should expect (SOW + pricing sheet + invoice terms).

Best,
Laura Bennett
